newQuestions.note: Nearly half of Americans admit to peeing in the shower at some point during the year — a quarter do it regularly.
newQuestions.source: Talker Research survey of 2,000 US adults, Feb 2025: 45% pee in the shower at some point during the year, 24% regularly.
newQuestions.text: What % of people pee in the shower?

newQuestions.note: Over two-thirds of Americans admit to scrolling on the toilet.
newQuestions.source: Reviews.org 2026 Cell Phone Usage Stats, survey of ~1,000 US adults, Q4 2025: 67.9% use their phone on the toilet.
newQuestions.text: What % of people use their phone on the toilet?

newQuestions.note: More than a third of Americans routinely drift off with the TV still on.
newQuestions.source: Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center / Harris Poll, July 2022, 2,040 US adults: 37% fall asleep with the TV on.
newQuestions.text: What % of people fall asleep with the TV on?

newQuestions.note: Most pet owners chat with their animals as if they were people — dog owners (83%) slightly more than cat owners (68%).
newQuestions.source: Preply survey of 1,500 American pet owners, July 2023: 84% regularly talk to their pets like fellow humans.
newQuestions.text: What % of pet owners talk to their pets like fellow humans?

newQuestions.note: Nearly 9 in 10 Americans have a show they return to again and again when times get tough.
newQuestions.source: CableTV.com survey of 1,000 Americans, 2023: 87% say they have a comfort show they turn to again and again.
newQuestions.text: What % of people have a comfort show they rewatch when stressed?

newQuestions.note: Most Americans have texted someone sitting in the very same room as them.
newQuestions.source: Reviews.org 2026 Cell Phone Usage Stats, survey of ~1,000 US adults, Q4 2025: 60% have texted someone in the same room.
newQuestions.text: What % of people have texted someone in the same room as them?

newQuestions.note: Nearly three-quarters of people sleep with their phone within arm's reach.
newQuestions.source: Asurion 2022 survey of ~2,000 US adults: 71% sleep with their phone within arm's reach.
newQuestions.text: What % of people sleep with their phone within arm's reach?

results.reason: YouGov's Oct 2025 poll (1,126 US adults) found exactly 48% like or love pineapple on pizza, matching the bank's 48 — the question wording ("think pineapple belongs") is a fair paraphrase of liking it on pizza.
results.source: YouGov Oct 2025 poll of 1,126 US adults: 48% like or love pineapple on pizza, 44% dislike or hate it.

results.reason: Bank's 71% is far off the only named-survey figure: Pew's 2011 study found just 13% of cell owners had faked being on the phone to avoid interaction (30% among 18-29s).
results.source: Pew Internet & American Life Project 2011 survey of 2,277 US adults: 13% of cell owners had pretended to be using their phone to avoid interaction.

results.reason: Bank's 84% matches the within-10-minutes figure, not 5 minutes. Asurion's 2022 survey found 75% check within 5 minutes of waking (89% within 10).
results.source: Asurion 2022 survey of ~2,000 US adults: 75% check their phone within 5 minutes of waking up.

results.reason: YouGov's Oct 2024 movie-etiquette poll (1,134 US adults) asked exactly this: 39% have fallen asleep during a movie in a theater, not 57%.
results.source: YouGov Oct 2024 poll of 1,134 US adults: 39% have fallen asleep during a movie in a theater.

results.reason: Bank's 82% is unsupported. Pew's most recent measure (Apr-May 2013) found 56% of internet users had used a search engine to look up their own name (57% in 2009). Figure is among internet users, not all people.
results.source: Pew Research Center survey, Apr-May 2013: 56% of internet users have used a search engine to look up their own name.

results.newText: What % of Americans pick cold pizza over standard breakfast foods?
results.reason: No published survey measures reheating pizza and calling it breakfast. Reframed to the closest real stat: Slice's survey found 53% of Americans pick cold pizza over standard breakfast foods (eggs, bacon, toast, etc.).
results.source: Slice survey of Americans (reported via Delish/Mashed): 53% pick cold pizza for breakfast over standard breakfast foods.

results.reason: Bank's 88% understates it. Junk King's 2024 survey found 95% of Americans have at least one junk drawer. (The "couldn't fully explain" phrasing is flavor; the drawer itself is the measured behavior.)
results.source: Junk King 2024 survey: 95% of Americans admit to having at least one junk drawer in their home.

results.reason: Bank's 76% is unsupported. Sky Mobile's Apr 2025 survey of 2,000 Brits found sending a text to the wrong person was the top phone faux pas at 61%.
results.source: Sky Mobile survey of 2,000 UK adults, Apr 2025: 61% have sent a text to the wrong person.

results.reason: Bank's 64% is unsupported — published figures range wildly (10% to 89%) depending on wording. The cleanest named survey is Mira/YouGov (2,061 UK adults, Apr 2018): 1 in 10 sing in the shower.
results.source: Mira Showers / YouGov survey of 2,061 UK adults, Apr 2018: 1 in 10 people sing in the shower.

results.reason: Bank's 44% is close but the named survey says 40%: MSC Cruises UK's 2017 study of 2,000 Brits found four in ten had claimed to have seen a film they'd never seen.
results.source: MSC Cruises UK study of 2,000 Brits, 2017: 40% had claimed to have seen a film they have never seen.

results.reason: Bank's 52% is unsupported. Bosch's Mar 2025 survey of 2,000 UK adults found 73% would eat food that had fallen on the floor if they could pick it up quickly (45% follow the five-second rule specifically).
results.source: Bosch survey of 2,000 UK adults, Mar 2025: 73% would eat food that had fallen on the floor if retrieved quickly.

results.reason: Searched for surveys on waving back at someone who was not waving at you ("waved back at someone who wasn't waving", "mistaken wave survey"). Found only anecdotes, forum threads, and a runner's Instagram wave-back experiment — no published survey measures this exact behavior, so it cannot be kept or honestly reframed.

results.newText: What % of people set multiple alarms to wake up?
results.reason: No published stat measures setting MORE THAN THREE alarms specifically. Reframed to the closest real behavior: a University of Notre Dame study (450 working professionals tracked 10 months) found 57% were habitual snoozers, defined as using multiple alarms to accomplish waking.
results.source: University of Notre Dame snoozing study (450 professionals, 10 months): 57% were habitual snoozers, defined as using multiple alarms to wake.

results.newText: What % of people haven't killed a houseplant in the last two years?
results.reason: No credible published stat measures keeping a plant alive for more than a year as a % of people (one weak furniture-retailer claim of 2.3% could not be verified). Reframed to Blooming Artificial's survey of 1,000+ UK adults: 40% had not killed a houseplant in the last two years.
results.source: Blooming Artificial survey of 1,000+ UK adults, 2024: 40% had not killed a houseplant in the last two years.

results.reason: Deloitte's 2017 Global Mobile Consumer Survey (2,000 US adults) found exactly 9% read terms and conditions in full before agreeing — matches the bank's 9.
results.source: Deloitte Global Mobile Consumer Survey 2017, 2,000 US adults: 9% read terms and conditions in full before agreeing (91% accept without reading).

results.newText: What % of people couldn't recall a friend's phone number without looking it up?
results.reason: No published survey asks about a childhood best friend's phone number specifically. Reframed to Kaspersky Lab's 2015 digital-amnesia study (1,000+ US adults): 51.4% could not call their friends without looking up the number.
results.source: Kaspersky Lab digital amnesia study, 2015, 1,000+ US adults: 51.4% were unable to call their friends without looking up the number.

results.newText: What % of Facebook users would give up Facebook for a month for $500?
results.reason: No published survey asks about giving up all social media for $500. Reframed to the peer-reviewed Allcott et al. experiment: almost 20% of Facebook users valued a month off Facebook at over $500, so ~80% would accept $500 or less.
results.source: Allcott, Braghieri, Eichmeyer & Gentzkow, American Economic Review 2020 (NBER WP 25514, 2,743 US Facebook users): almost 20% had willingness-to-accept over $500 to deactivate for four weeks, median $100.

results.newText: What % of millennials have a 'chair' covered in clothes right now?
results.reason: No published survey measures the chair-of-clothes habit across all people. Reframed to the named figure: Unilever's 2018 market research found 60% of millennials have a 'chairdrobe' — a chair covered in lightly worn clothes.
results.source: Unilever market research, 2018 (reported by Reuters): 60% of millennials have a 'chairdrobe'.

results.reason: Bank's 66% is unsupported. WebMD, citing a study of adults, reports 25% of adults talk to themselves out loud (96% have an internal dialogue). Note: WebMD does not name the underlying study, so this is the weakest 'correct' in the set — flag for replacement if a named survey surfaces.
results.source: WebMD citing a study of adults: 25% of adults talk to themselves out loud.

results.reason: Bank's 61% is close but the best named US survey says 58%: PhotoAid's Dec 2024 survey of 1,095 Americans found 58% prefer window seats (28% middle, 12% aisle).
results.source: PhotoAid survey of 1,095 US adults, Dec 2024: 58% prefer window seats.

results.newText: What % of people have rewatched an entire TV series from start to finish?
results.reason: No published survey measures rewatching a favorite show more than three times. Reframed to Brightcove/OnePoll's Jul 2018 poll of 2,000 UK adults: 45% had viewed an entire series or box set from start to finish again.
results.source: Brightcove / OnePoll poll of 2,000 UK adults, Jul 2018: 45% had rewatched an entire series from start to finish.

results.reason: Bank's 31% is close. Pew Research Center's survey of nearly 5,000 US adults found 34% of people in relationships have looked through their partner's phone without permission (42% of women, 25% of men).
results.source: Pew Research Center survey of ~5,000 US adults: 34% of people in relationships have snooped on their partner's phone without permission.

results.reason: Bank's 77% is close. YouGov's Apr 2023 pizza poll (1,000 US adults) asked exactly this: 79% typically eat the crust of their pizza.
results.source: YouGov pizza poll, Apr 11-13 2023, 1,000 US adults: 79% typically eat the crust of their pizza.

results.reason: Bank's 86% is unsupported. Capital One Shopping's 2025 data found 70% of consumers have impulsively bought an item specifically because it was on sale — the single biggest impulse-buy trigger.
results.source: Capital One Shopping impulse-buying data, 2025: 70% of consumers have impulsively bought an item because it was on sale.

results.reason: Searched for surveys on laughing at a funeral / fighting off laughter at a funeral ("laughing at funeral survey percentage", "inappropriate laughter funeral"). Found only psychology explainers (Bonanno & Keltner 1997 on Duchenne laughter in bereavement, Milgram nervous laughter) and etiquette articles — no published survey gives a % of people who have fought off laughing at a funeral, so it cannot be kept.

Published estimates for naming a car vary wildly (25%-56% across surveys), so the bank's 50% was a coin flip. The most recent named US survey — Talker Research for Ziebart, Jun 2025, 2,000 US car owners — found 21% have given their car a name.
results.source: Talker Research / Ziebart survey of 2,000 US car owners, Jun 2025: 21% have bestowed their car with a name.

results.reason: Bank's 45% is unsupported for the exact behavior. Vodafone/Bryter's 2015 survey of 2,103 UK residents found 30% have missed their stop on public transport (headline: one in three slept through their stop on a commute due to tiredness).
results.source: Vodafone / Bryter survey of 2,103 UK residents, Sep 2015: 30% have missed their stop on public transport; one in three have slept through their stop.
